Subject: CAIQ: initial tenant-level evidence ask and batch constraints

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start the CAIQ review for Helix Health's purchasing committee, the audit team has a couple of specific asks around tenant-level proofing and how you bundle artifacts for bulk upload into our portal. Can you provide:

- A short list of CAIQ claims where tenant isolation is the primary control (we need the claim IDs and short rationale).
- A sample of runtime evidence (logs/key retention) showing per-tenant segregation for inference requests.
- An explanation of how you batch artifacts for DocuSign/portal ingestion — we have file size limits and prefer CSV manifest + zipped artifacts.

Our timeline is tight: evidence needs to be uploaded to the portal by 2026-11-22. If you can send a staging package and a brief walkthrough this week, that would help.

Olivia Chen
Head of Security Assurance
Helix Health
--

Olivia — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it. Quick plan below: 

1) Tenant proof claims list: we will provide a claims snapshot (CSV + PDF) that maps CAIQ questions to our tenant-isolation artifacts (e.g., per-tenant API keys, network ACLs, namespace-level logs). Expect the file redwood_caiq_claims_snapshot_20261115.pdf.

2) Runtime evidence sample: attaching a small, redacted KV cache / request log sample that shows tenant IDs and routing. That will be kv-cache-log-sample_20261114.txt.

3) Batch/manifest approach: we typically send a manifest.csv + zipped artifacts. We'll prepare a one-page guidance doc for Helix's portal limits.

Can we set a 30-minute walkthrough on 2026-11-17 10:00 PT to walk your audit team through the package and manifesto? Marissa (CS lead) and Priya (security SME) will join.

Action items for us: Hannah to assemble package, Marissa to prepare upload checklist, Priya to prepare attestation language.

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks all. Quick technical clarifications for audit traceability: 

- Mapping: we reference the CCMS families that matter most to tenant proofing: "Identity & Access Management (IAM)", "Data Protection & Privacy", and "Infrastructure & Network Segmentation". Example internal labels in our claims snapshot: IAM-RTN-01, NET-SGT-03, DP-RET-02.
- Evidence lifetimes: logs are retained for 90 days by default in hosted; Dedicated customers can request extended retention windows (contracted). If Helix needs 365-day retention for the audit window, we need procurement approval.
- Per-tenant keys: tenant API keys are rotated every 30 days; HSM-wrapped keys are used for tenant-level service credentials.

Olivia — confirm if you need extended retention or a timeboxed export rather than our standard 90-day sample. If extended retention is required for the CAIQ submission, I'll start the intake with our contracts team.

Priya Natarajan
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
